content.title: About
content.content: Cornmeal stick, Puerto Rican style are crunchy corn sticks made according to a traditional Puerto Rican recipe. A dough of cornmeal, water, salt and spices is shaped into thin sticks and fried until golden. They have a light corn aroma, a mildly salty flavor and a crisp texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The traditional recipe dates back to the early 20th century as a street snack in San Juan.
The cornmeal used is usually "masa harina," finely ground and often calcium‑enriched.
Sticks are commonly served with "mojo" or "mari" sauces – typical Puerto Rican tomato‑based sauces.
In Puerto Rico they are called "corn sticks" or "corn chips," but differ from American corn chips by having a softer interior.
They are a popular snack during festivals and carnivals.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Cornmeal provides slow‑releasing energy, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When baked rather than deep‑fried, the sticks contain relatively little fat compared with many other snack foods.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Corn supplies dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, niacin and folate in corn aid metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Cornmeal is naturally gluten‑free, making the product suitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: High salt levels can raise blood pressure; consume in moderation.

items.title: Calorie density when fried
items.content: Deep‑frying significantly increases the calorie count.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the sticks as a snack on their own, dip them in sauces (mojo, guacamole, salsa) or add them to salads for crunch. They are convenient for picnics, trips, and outdoor activities.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For storage longer than two weeks, keep refrigerated to maintain crispness and prevent mold.
